title: Parametric Equations
standard_text: P.3A graph a set of parametric equations; P.3B convert parametric equations into rectangular relations and convert rectangular relations into parametric equations; P.3C use parametric equations to model and solve mathematical and real-world problems
meta_desc: Free Precalculus worksheets on parametric equations for Texas TEKS P.3A to P.3C: points, eliminating the parameter, writing parametric equations, motion and projectiles. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Solve one equation for t and substitute into the other.
key_sub: For y = f(x), let x = t and y = f(t).
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Parametric equations give x and y in terms of a third variable, the parameter t (often time).
  • To plot, make a table of t, x and y. The curve has a direction as t increases.
  • To eliminate the parameter, solve one equation for t and substitute, or use cos2 t + sin2 t = 1.
  • To write parametric equations for y = f(x), let x = t and y = f(t).

Examples

Example

x = t + 2, y = t2 − 1

t = x − 2

Answer: y = (x − 2)2 − 1

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Using t in only one equationPut t into both.
Solving for t in the harder equationUse the simpler one.
Landing time as distanceFind x at that time.
